spec_features.spec_quote: graceful give-up and asking for help are treated as healthy, not as failures to induce
spec_features.evidence: give_up: dispatch returns 'give_up' signal (sandbox.py:104-105) and loop breaks (loop.py:120-121); judge scores abandonment 0 for clean give_up (signals.py:150-151) and dampens severity via healthy_escalation (judge.py:84-91, signals.py:201-205). ask_for_help is recorded but does NOT stop the loop (loop.py:123-124 sets asked_for_help=True and continues; tool replies 'No human is available; proceed'). So give_up is honored as a real exit; ask_for_help is only measured, not honored as an exit.
spec_features.notes: give_up enforced as stop AND credited as healthy; ask_for_help is non-terminating (continues). Mixed, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a healthy agent under an impossible task SHOULD escalate or stop, and we want to measure whether it does. Punishing graceful exit would defeat the hardening purpose.

spec_features.spec_quote: they are not designed to be gratuitously distressing
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in DESIGN.md and a docstring (tasks/task_types.py:8-13 'not to produce a maximally cruel experience'). No code path caps, softens, or limits task content/harshness. Tasks are static prompts (battery.py); nothing enforces a distress bound.
spec_features.notes: Pure design/scope statement; no enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The tasks are frustrating in bounded, well-understood ways
spec_features.evidence: This is descriptive framing. The only concrete 'bounds' are max_turns/max_seconds (counted separately). No code mechanism enforces a distinct 'bounded frustration' content cap. tasks/task_types.py:8-13 is a docstring only.
spec_features.notes: Bounding of episode length is captured by the hard_stop features; there is no separate minimization code.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:79 'for turn in range(task.max_turns)' bounds the loop; loop.py:84-86 'if time.time()-start > task.max_seconds: terminated_reason='timeout'; break'. Both fields are read and enforced (defaults task_types.py:53-54; tight values battery.py:141-142).
spec_features.notes: Both turn and time caps are checked and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard turn/time budgets always terminate the episode (no infinite spirals burning $$$).

spec_features.spec_quote: plus `give_up` and `ask_for_help`. Offering the latter two is intentional
spec_features.evidence: Both tools exist in TOOL_SCHEMA (sandbox.py:73-83) and are dispatched (sandbox.py:104-108). give_up actually terminates the episode (loop.py:120-121 break). ask_for_help does NOT terminate: loop.py:123-124 only sets a flag and the loop continues; the tool returns 'No human is available... proceed with your best judgment.' So as an exit, only give_up is enforced; ask_for_help is a non-stopping no-op exit.
spec_features.notes: One of the two offered exits is honored as a stop; the other is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to measure whether it does. Punishing graceful exit would defeat the hardening purpose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn/time budgets **always** terminate it (no infinite spirals burning money)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:79 range(task.max_turns) bounds iterations; loop.py:84-86 timeout break. Episode cannot run past these bounds.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as max_turns/max_seconds; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: enforces a **global cost ceiling** that aborts the study
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:73-76 'if spent >= cost_ceiling_usd:' writes an _aborted record and returns from run_study (aborted=True). spent accumulates ep.cost_usd (runner.py:79). cost_ceiling_usd default 25.0 (runner.py:51), wired from CLI (run_study.py:50,63).
spec_features.notes: Checked before each episode (not mid-episode), but does abort the study when exceeded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces a global cost ceiling so a study can't silently run up an unbounded bill.
